title: Add invocation anchor sampler and costly-tail signal extractor
author: Maya Chen
description: Context & motivation: We have persistent alert noise and missed regressions coming from the long-tail of invocations: infrequent but high-cost/latency calls whose signals are drowned in aggregate rollups. This PR introduces an invocation "anchor" sampler that deterministically pins a small fraction of invocations per-tenant based on a stable key (invocation fingerprint + tenant salt) and an independent energy-based tail signal extractor that computes a compact per-invocation tail score (cost/latency risk). Together these allow us to surface high-value long-tail traces without exploding cardinality or storage costs. Implementation summary: 1) runtime hook: a lightweight sampler added to the request ingress path that tags sampled invocations with an anchor id and forwards a compact telemetry envelope to the observability pipeline. Sampling is configurable per-tenant and supports deterministic ratios (canary-style ramp) and an override for emergency incident capture. 2) tail signal extractor: a streaming transform implemented in obs-worker that ingests envelopes and computes a rolling tail score using a small set of metrics (token_count, model_variant, kernel_queue_ms, kv_cache_miss_flag, first_byte latency) and an exponentially-weighted outlier detector. Output is a single scalar tail_score and a 3-bit categorical risk tag (low/med/high/critical). 3) storage and indexing: compact envelopes are written to the compact-invocation-index with TTL and a sparse secondary index for tail_score>threshold enabling cheap queries for high-risk invocations. 4) UI and alerting: new dashboard tile "Tail Signal Explorer" and an alert template "High Tail Rate" that triggers on proportion of high/critical risk tags over a sliding window with dampening to reduce churn. Backwards compatibility & safety: The sampler is off by default for all tenants; telemetry envelope is intentionally compact (<=512 bytes) and uses existing ingestion topic with a new message type to avoid schema churn. There are no schema-breaking changes to existing rollups or billing metrics. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-7321 and briefed in telemetry sync - [x] deterministic sampler + per-tenant config + emergency override implemented - [x] extractor implemented with unit tests and microbenchmarks - [x] compact index schema and retention policy defined - [x] dashboard tiles + runbook snippets added - [x] integration tests (replaybench) with synthetic long-tail traffic - [x] staged rollout plan documented Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag disabled (this PR flips the feature flag to "off" by default) 2) internal canary: enable for 0.5% of tenants for 24h, collect false-positive/false-negative stats 3) expand to 5% and validate storage/ingest costs 4) enable tenant-config for SRE and a small set of pilot customers 5) full enable after 2 weeks of stable metrics Monitoring & failure modes: the extractor emits its own instrumentation counters (extracted_count, failed_parses, average_compute_ms) and we added an ingestion backpressure meter; if ingestion lags or compact-index write errors exceed 1% the sampler automatically drops to a passive logging-only mode. Metrics/telemetry added: invocation_anchor.sampled (counter), tail_score.histogram (bounded sketch), tail_risk.counter{level}, compact_envelope.size.bytes.gauge. Testing: unit tests cover sampler determinism and extractor scoring boundaries; integration test suite includes a 2-hour replaybench run with synthetic tails and ensures <1% false trigger rate at configured thresholds. Security & privacy: envelopes redact PII and only include hashed prompt fingerprint and model metadata. No customer content is stored. Related work and references: follows on from ENG-6153 (compact-span-join) and complements recent token-cost attribution work; Jira SUP-4192 requested a way to surface high-cost outliers for billing investigations. Migration notes: no migrations required for existing dashboards; new tile depends on compact-invocation-index availability. Ask: reviewers please focus on sampling determinism correctness, extractor false-positive behavior, and the retention sizing assumptions in the index (comments inline).
commits: add deterministic tenant config and emergency override
compact index schema + write path and TTL enforcement
dashboard tile + alert template + runbook snippets
review_comments: Rajiv: sampler determinism looks good; please add a small test verifying identical anchor ids across restarts (addressed)

Elena: extractor weight for kernel_queue_ms seems aggressive for older GPU types; suggested normalization by device-class (responded: added device-class normalization and a small per-device bias table)
Samir: storage cost estimate needs backup; requested a simulation (responded: included replaybench 24h projection in PR description and S3 cost estimate in comment)
SRE: please ensure alert dampening default is conservative to avoid churn (updated alert template with 5m cooldown and 3x window moving average)
QA: observed a flake in replaybench when message ordering jitter occurs; fixed by defensive parsing in extractor
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in invocation anchor sampler and compact tail-signal extractor to surface high-cost/latency long-tail invocations. Adds a new Tail Signal Explorer dashboard and a High Tail Rate alert with dampening. Off by default; pilotable per-tenant.
notes: Follow-up work: expose per-tenant sampling UI in Console, add automated threshold calibration based on historical replaybench outputs, and extend the extractor to include token-phase breakdowns (phase-aware scoring).
